parsed_result.title: Parsing Two-Column Papers Without Crossing the Gutter
parsed_result.abstract: Two-column scientific layouts are common in engineering and life-science publishing, and naive text extraction walks straight across the gutter. This synthetic manuscript exercises a parser on a controllable layout: spanning title, spanning abstract, two body columns, a full-width table, a numbered display equation, a figure caption and a reference list. The intended reading order is column-major inside each band and top-to-bottom across bands. Margins carry a running banner and a folio that must never reach the body text.

sections.heading: 1. Column Ordering
sections.content: Reading order is a property of the layout, not of the content stream. A parser that sorts glyphs by their y coordinate alone will interleave the left and right columns line by line, producing sentences that alternate between two unrelated paragraphs. Sorting by x first is equally wrong, because it destroys the vertical flow inside a column. The correct model cuts the page into bands at spanning elements and then reads each column of a band from top to bottom.

sections.heading: 2. Table Reconstruction
sections.content:
Table reconstruction needs cell geometry rather than whitespace heuristics. When a tabular block is drawn without ruling lines, the only reliable signal is the alignment of cell boxes across rows, combined with the vertical gaps between cells inside a row. Column anchors derived from those boxes let a grid be rebuilt as Markdown, which is what downstream parameter extraction expects.

Figure 1. Reading order of a band that contains a spanning table.

Columns are read left to right inside each band.
